comments.body:
Lang-nominating, since if-let guards are now stable in nightly, and is on its way to being actually stable on stable.

~~One possibility is destabilizing if-let guards only when used in combination with or-patterns.~~
I am quite confused because we do emit false edges for all these cases, so borrowck should not be seeing a difference between these cases.

As for what the correct behavior should be, I have two ideas.
- The current behavior.
- We make ref-for-guard bindings[^1] for by-move bindings assigned in `if let` guards if there's additional conditions, then move into the actual bindings for the arm if the whole guard succeeds[^2]. This would make `fails` compile, but it'd be an error to move out of a by-move binding later in the guard (similar to how you can't move out of the arm's pattern's by-move bindings in a guard).

I'm leaning towards keeping things as-is for simplicity. Notably, it's already possible to run into move errors in guards; as far as I can tell, `if let` guards are only unique in that bindings can be assigned after the guard succeeds. I don't think it's worth making `if let` guards more special than they are to trade some move errors for other move errors. But I could maybe be convinced if there's a good argument for that. The one thing I really don't want is to add a false edge to treat bindings in the final condition of an `if let` guard chain as if they're fallible (to make `works2` fail).

If we keep things as they are now, maybe we could have diagnostics to encourage using by-ref bindings in `let` chains.

[^1]: https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/expressions/match-expr.html#r-expr.match.guard.shared-ref
[^2]: https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/expressions/match-expr.html#r-expr.match.guard.value

I see. My mental rule is that borrowck/moveck should view the control-flow inside matches as as opaque as possible, so I'd personally add a false edge at the end of every guard too, which would happen after any guard-induced bindings are set up. This would make `works2` error.

Maybe I could be convinced of that too ^^ I think at the time I was thinking of the pattern-match as being the guard and the bindings as not being part of the guard, but thinking about it again, that makes less sense than both of those being the guard, yeah.
I've come around on the false edge; it makes a lot more sense to treat a guard's bindings as part of the guard. Here's a PR: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/153337
Unnominated and nominated the PR isntead for t-lang consideration.

This was discussed on the PR, see there for more interesting examples. This was raised in t-lang meeting and meeting consensus was that current behavior is fine (as per [this comment](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/153337#issuecomment-3998915995)).

title: Odd behavior with by-move `if let` guards
